writes.rule: Per subtopic seen: pMastery 0.7 if right at D2/D3, 0.55 if right at D1, 0.25 if wrong; level L0-L3 from the ladder step reached
Prerequisite-gap index = 100 x weighted misses / weighted items seen in slots 1-4, averaged over groups
Groups with the highest Part A percent (top 1-2, only if >= 65%)
Groups with the lowest Part A percent (bottom 1-2, only if < 65%)
Calibration = 1 - mean |confidence/5 - correct| over Part A (feeds the first MCI reading)
Highest difficulty answered correctly twice in a row: D1 low, D2 medium, D3 high
Verbal reasoning = percent of Part B verbal items right
Numerical reasoning = percent of Part B numerical items right
Abstract reasoning = percent of Part B abstract items right
Spatial reasoning = percent of Part B spatial items right
Logical deduction = percent right on Part B items tagged p65
Numeracy fluency = numerical percent scaled by speed (right answers under target time count 1.2x, max 100)
Processing speed = 100 x share of Part B items answered right within target seconds
RIASEC profile: each career-interest item scored 1-5; letter score = mean of its 2 items; top 3 letters form the code (e.g. IRC)

items.stem: Which of these numbers is a perfect square?
items.markingKey: C. 196. 14 x 14 = 196; the others are not the square of any whole number
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: multiplication facts and squares of numbers

items.stem: Which shows 36 written as a product of prime factors?
items.markingKey: A. 2 x 2 x 3 x 3. 4, 6 and 9 are not prime; 36 = 2 x 2 x 3 x 3
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 6-7: factors, primes and prime factorisation

items.stem: The prime factorisation of 180 is
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 6-7: factors, primes and prime factorisation

items.stem: 5⁴ means
items.markingKey: C. 5 x 5 x 5 x 5. The exponent 4 says how many 5s are multiplied
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: exponents and powers

items.stem: What is the value of 2⁵?
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: exponents and powers

items.stem: Which is greater, 3⁴ or 4³, and by how much?
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: exponents and powers

items.markingKey: C. -3. Start at -8 and move 5 to the right on the number line
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: integers and fractions, four operations

items.markingKey: C. 1/12. Common denominator 12: 9/12 - 8/12 = 1/12
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: integers and fractions, four operations

items.stem: A jug holds 2 1/2 litres of milk. 3/4 litre is used for tea and 1 1/3 litres for a pudding. How much milk is left?
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: integers and fractions, four operations

items.stem: Identify the rational number.
items.markingKey: A. -3/5. A rational number can be written as a fraction of integers

items.stem: Order from smallest to largest: -0.5, 1/3, -2/3, 0.3
Which is larger, 5/8 or 0.6, and by how much?
Simplify 10³ x 10².
items.subtopicHint: Laws of exponents and scientific notation
items.markingKey: A. 10⁵. Same base: add the exponents

items.stem: The distance from Earth to the Sun is about 150 000 000 km. Write this in scientific notation.
items.subtopicHint: Laws of exponents and scientific notation
items.markingKey: B. 1.5 x 10⁸ km. Move the decimal point 8 places

items.stem: Light travels about 3 x 10⁵ km every second. About how long does sunlight take to travel 1.5 x 10⁸ km to Earth?
items.subtopicHint: Laws of exponents and scientific notation

items.stem: What is 15% of 200?
A jacket costs 80 euros and is reduced by 25%. What is the new price?
A town's population grew from 40 000 to 46 000. What is the percentage increase?
items.markingKey: B. 15%. Increase 6 000 ÷ original 40 000 = 0.15

items.stem: Solve x + 7 = 12.
items.markingKey: A. 5. Subtract 7 from both sides

items.stem: Solve 3x - 4 = 11.
items.markingKey: C. 5. Add 4: 3x = 15, so x = 5

items.stem: Solve 2(x + 3) = 4x - 8.
A potted plant is kept in a dark cupboard for 3 days. One leaf is then tested with iodine. What do you expect, and why?
items.answer: No blue-black colour, because no starch was made without light
options: No blue-black colour, because iodine reacts only with sugar
No blue-black colour, because no starch was made without light
Blue-black colour, because the plant made starch from soil water
Blue-black colour, because leaves always store starch
items.markingKey: B. No blue-black colour, because no starch was made without light. Iodine turns blue-black with starch; without light the plant uses up its starch and cannot make more
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: nutrition in plants (photosynthesis)

items.stem: In a circuit diagram, a long line drawn next to a short line stands for
items.markingKey: D. A cell. The long line is the positive terminal of a cell
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: electric circuits and their components

items.stem: A bulb does not glow when a rubber eraser closes the gap in a circuit, but glows with a steel key. This shows that
items.answer: steel is a conductor and rubber is an insulator
options: steel is a conductor and rubber is an insulator
both are conductors but rubber is weaker
rubber is a conductor and steel is an insulator
items.markingKey: A. steel is a conductor and rubber is an insulator. Current flows through conductors such as metals, not through insulators such as rubber
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: electric circuits and their components

items.stem: In an experiment, the factor you deliberately change is called the
items.markingKey: D. independent variable. You change the independent variable and measure the dependent one
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: planning a fair investigation

items.stem: A student wants to test whether salt makes ice melt faster. What must stay the same in both cups?
items.answer: The size of the ice cubes and the room temperature
options: Only the time she checks the result
The size of the ice cubes and the room temperature
items.markingKey: C. The size of the ice cubes and the room temperature. Only one factor (salt) should change; everything else is controlled
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: planning a fair investigation

items.stem: A student says plants grow taller with music. He plays music to one plant on a sunny window and keeps another plant, without music, in a dark corner. What is wrong with his test?
items.answer: Two factors (music and light) changed, so he cannot tell which caused the difference
options: He should have used three plants with music
Two factors (music and light) changed, so he cannot tell which caused the difference
Plants cannot hear, so no test is needed
He should measure the leaves, not the height
items.markingKey: B. Two factors (music and light) changed, so he cannot tell which caused the difference. A fair test changes one variable at a time
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: planning a fair investigation

items.stem: Digestion of starch begins in the
items.markingKey: C. mouth. Saliva contains an enzyme that starts breaking starch down
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: nutrition in animals (human digestive system)

items.stem: Why is the inner wall of the small intestine covered with finger-like villi?
items.answer: They increase the surface area for absorbing digested food
options: They increase the surface area for absorbing digested food
They push food back to the stomach
items.markingKey: A. They increase the surface area for absorbing digested food. More surface means faster absorption into the blood
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: nutrition in animals (human digestive system)

items.stem: A person whose gall bladder was removed is advised to eat less oily food. Which reason fits best?
items.answer: Bile, which breaks fat into small droplets, is no longer stored and released in large amounts
options: The stomach can no longer make acid
Fat is digested only in the gall bladder
Bile, which breaks fat into small droplets, is no longer stored and released in large amounts
items.markingKey: C. Bile, which breaks fat into small droplets, is no longer stored and released in large amounts. The gall bladder stores bile; without it less bile is available at mealtimes to emulsify fat
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: nutrition in animals (human digestive system)

items.stem: Identify the structure found in plant cells but not in animal cells.
items.markingKey: A. Cell wall. Plant cells have a cellulose cell wall (and chloroplasts and a large vacuole)

items.stem: Outline the function of mitochondria.
items.answer: They release energy from glucose in respiration
options: They control what enters the cell
They release energy from glucose in respiration
items.markingKey: C. They release energy from glucose in respiration. Mitochondria are the site of aerobic respiration

items.stem: Root cells of a plant have no chloroplasts. Explain why.
items.answer: Roots are underground without light, so they cannot photosynthesise
options: Roots need to stay white to be strong
Chloroplasts are only made in flowers
Roots are underground without light, so they cannot photosynthesise
items.markingKey: C. Roots are underground without light, so they cannot photosynthesise. Chloroplasts are only useful where light reaches

items.stem: Which blood vessels carry blood away from the heart?
items.markingKey: B. arteries. Arteries carry blood away; veins return it

items.stem: Explain why the wall of the left ventricle is thicker than the wall of the right ventricle.
items.answer: It pumps blood around the whole body, which needs more force
options: It pumps blood only to the lungs
It receives blood from the body
It pumps blood around the whole body, which needs more force
items.markingKey: C. It pumps blood around the whole body, which needs more force. The right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs

items.stem: During exercise your heart rate increases. Which explanation is best?
items.answer: Muscles need oxygen and glucose delivered faster for respiration
options: Muscles need oxygen and glucose delivered faster for respiration
The lungs stop working during exercise
The heart needs to cool down
items.markingKey: A. Muscles need oxygen and glucose delivered faster for respiration. Working muscles respire faster

items.stem: In which state are particles closest together and only vibrating in fixed positions?
items.markingKey: D. solid. Solids have a fixed shape because particles cannot move past each other

items.stem: Explain why a gas can be compressed but a solid cannot easily be compressed.
items.answer: Gas particles have large spaces between them
options: Gas particles have large spaces between them
items.markingKey: B. Gas particles have large spaces between them. Compression pushes particles into the gaps

items.stem: A balloon left in a hot car expands. Explain this using the particle model.
items.answer: The particles gain kinetic energy, move faster and hit the balloon wall harder and more often
options: Heat adds new particles to the balloon
The rubber shrinks in the heat
The particles grow larger when heated
The particles gain kinetic energy, move faster and hit the balloon wall harder and more often
items.markingKey: D. The particles gain kinetic energy, move faster and hit the balloon wall harder and more often. Particles do not change size; their motion changes

items.stem: Speed is calculated as
items.subtopicHint: Forces and motion: speed and balanced forces
items.markingKey: A. distance ÷ time. v = d / t

items.stem: A cyclist travels 18 km in 45 minutes. What is the average speed?
items.subtopicHint: Forces and motion: speed and balanced forces

items.stem: A moving box is pushed to the right with 50 N while friction acts to the left with 50 N. Describe its motion.
items.answer: It keeps moving at a constant speed
items.subtopicHint: Forces and motion: speed and balanced forces
options: It keeps moving at a constant speed
items.markingKey: A. It keeps moving at a constant speed. Balanced forces mean no change in motion

items.stem: Read: 'The old fort looked desolate; no one had visited it in years.' What does 'desolate' most likely mean?
items.markingKey: A. empty and lonely. 'No one had visited it in years' signals emptiness
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: working out word meaning from context

items.stem: Choose the correct word: Yesterday, Kabir ___ his bicycle to school.
items.markingKey: A. rode. 'Yesterday' needs the simple past
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: simple past and past continuous

items.stem: Choose the correct words: When the lights went out, we ___ dinner.
items.markingKey: A. were having. An action in progress in the past uses the past continuous
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: simple past and past continuous

items.stem: Choose the correct word: Each of the students ___ a library card.
items.markingKey: C. has. 'Each' is singular
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: subject-verb agreement

items.stem: Choose the correct word: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ aware of the change.
items.markingKey: C. were. With 'neither ... nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject, 'students'
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: subject-verb agreement

items.stem: Which sentence is correct?
items.answer: The bunch of keys was found under the sofa.
options: The bunch of keys was found under the sofa.
The bunch of keys were found under the sofa.
The bunch of keys are find under the sofa.
The bunch of keys have found under the sofa.
items.markingKey: A. The bunch of keys was found under the sofa.. The subject is 'bunch' (singular), not 'keys'
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: subject-verb agreement

items.stem: Read: "Bees visit flowers to collect nectar. As they move, pollen sticks to their bodies and is carried to other flowers. This helps plants make seeds." What is the passage mainly about?
items.answer: How bees help plants make seeds
options: How bees help plants make seeds
items.markingKey: A. How bees help plants make seeds. Every sentence builds towards pollination and seeds
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: reading for the main idea

items.stem: Read: "Arun practised the flute every evening, even when his friends called him out to play. At the school concert, the audience stood up and clapped for a long time." What is the main message?
options: Playing outside is a waste of time
items.markingKey: C. Steady practice leads to success. The practice in the first sentence explains the applause in the second
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: reading for the main idea

items.stem: Read: "Many cities now have car-free Sundays. Streets fill with cyclists, skaters and families. Shopkeepers first complained, but many now report more customers on foot." Which statement best sums up the passage?
items.answer: Car-free days, though doubted at first, benefit people and some businesses
options: Car-free days, though doubted at first, benefit people and some businesses
items.markingKey: C. Car-free days, though doubted at first, benefit people and some businesses. The summary must include both the early doubt and the later benefit
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: reading for the main idea

items.stem: A story narrated by a character who uses 'I' is written in
options: the third-person omniscient point of view
items.markingKey: D. the first-person point of view. 'I' marks a first-person narrator

items.stem: What is the main difference between a third-person limited narrator and a third-person omniscient narrator?
items.answer: A limited narrator follows one character's thoughts; an omniscient narrator can reveal any character's thoughts
options: A limited narrator uses 'I'; an omniscient narrator uses 'you'
A limited narrator follows one character's thoughts; an omniscient narrator can reveal any character's thoughts
items.markingKey: D. A limited narrator follows one character's thoughts; an omniscient narrator can reveal any character's thoughts. Omniscient means all-knowing

items.stem: Read: 'Of course I wasn't jealous, I told myself, slamming the door a little harder than I meant to.' Analyse what this reveals about the narrator.
items.answer: The narrator is unreliable: their action contradicts what they claim
options: The narrator is calm and honest
The narrator is talking to a friend
The narrator is unreliable: their action contradicts what they claim
items.markingKey: D. The narrator is unreliable: their action contradicts what they claim. 'I told myself' and the slammed door show self-deception

items.stem: In a text, tone means
items.answer: the writer's attitude towards the subject
options: the writer's attitude towards the subject
items.markingKey: A. the writer's attitude towards the subject. Tone is shown through word choice

items.stem: Which word best describes the tone of: 'Oh wonderful, another rainy holiday. Just what I wanted.'?
items.markingKey: A. sarcastic. The speaker says the opposite of what they mean

items.stem: A writer describes a market as 'a riot of colour, voices tumbling over each other'. Which mood is created?
items.markingKey: B. Lively, busy excitement. 'Riot of colour' and 'tumbling' voices suggest energy

items.stem: The main purpose of most advertisements is to
items.markingKey: C. persuade. Adverts aim to make you buy, join or act

items.stem: A poster uses bright cartoons, simple words and a chance to win a toy. Who is the most likely target audience?
items.markingKey: C. Young children. Every feature suits young readers

items.stem: A charity website tells one child's story instead of showing national statistics. Evaluate why the creators chose this.
items.answer: A personal story creates an emotional connection that can make readers more likely to donate
options: A personal story creates an emotional connection that can make readers more likely to donate
One story is more accurate than data
items.markingKey: B. A personal story creates an emotional connection that can make readers more likely to donate. Pathos often persuades more strongly than numbers

items.stem: A group of lines forming a section of a poem is called a
items.markingKey: D. stanza. Stanzas are the paragraphs of poetry

items.stem: Why might a poet repeat the same line at the end of every stanza?
items.answer: To emphasise a key idea and create rhythm
options: To emphasise a key idea and create rhythm
items.markingKey: A. To emphasise a key idea and create rhythm. A refrain reinforces meaning

items.stem: In a poem, the lines get shorter and shorter as a character falls asleep. Analyse the effect of this structure.
items.answer: The shrinking lines mirror the character slowing down and drifting off
options: It shows the poet ran out of ideas
It has no effect on meaning
The shrinking lines mirror the character slowing down and drifting off
items.markingKey: D. The shrinking lines mirror the character slowing down and drifting off. Form can enact meaning

items.stem: On a map with a scale of 1 : 50 000, two towns are 4 cm apart. What is the real distance between them?
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: map scale, grid references and distance

items.stem: A century is a period of
items.markingKey: C. 100 years. Centuries are 100-year periods
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: chronology, centuries and timelines

items.stem: Which order is correct, earliest first?
items.answer: Building of the Egyptian pyramids, the Roman Empire, the Industrial Revolution, the First World War
options: The Roman Empire, the Egyptian pyramids, the First World War, the Industrial Revolution
The Industrial Revolution, the Roman Empire, the Egyptian pyramids, the First World War
Building of the Egyptian pyramids, the Roman Empire, the Industrial Revolution, the First World War
The Egyptian pyramids, the Industrial Revolution, the Roman Empire, the First World War
items.markingKey: C. Building of the Egyptian pyramids, the Roman Empire, the Industrial Revolution, the First World War. About 2500 BCE, about 27 BCE to 476 CE, about 1760 to 1840, 1914 to 1918
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: chronology, centuries and timelines

items.stem: Which is a primary source about the First World War?
options: A website summary of the war
items.markingKey: D. A soldier's letter written in 1916. A primary source was made at the time by someone involved
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: using sources as evidence

items.stem: Why might a wartime newspaper be an unreliable source about the enemy country?
items.answer: It may be biased to support its own side
options: It may be biased to support its own side
It was printed on old paper
items.markingKey: A. It may be biased to support its own side. Wartime papers were often censored or used for propaganda
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: using sources as evidence

items.stem: Two historians disagree about why an empire collapsed. What is the best explanation?
items.answer: They use different evidence and give different weight to each cause
options: They use different evidence and give different weight to each cause
Empires collapse for only one reason
One of them must be lying
items.markingKey: A. They use different evidence and give different weight to each cause. Interpretations differ because evidence is selected and weighed differently
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: using sources as evidence

items.stem: Which of these is a basic human need?
items.markingKey: D. Clean water. Needs are essential for survival; the others are wants
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: human needs and why settlements grow where they do

items.stem: Why have many large cities grown up next to rivers or coasts?
items.answer: For water supply, transport and trade
options: It is cheaper to build on water
For water supply, transport and trade
items.markingKey: C. For water supply, transport and trade. Water routes carried goods and people
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: human needs and why settlements grow where they do

items.stem: A country has an ageing population. Which challenge is it most likely to face?
items.answer: More spending on pensions and healthcare, with fewer people of working age
options: More spending on pensions and healthcare, with fewer people of working age
items.markingKey: D. More spending on pensions and healthcare, with fewer people of working age. Older people need more care while the workforce shrinks
items.prerequisiteNote: Grade 7: human needs and why settlements grow where they do

items.stem: Migration means
items.answer: people moving from one place to live in another
options: people moving from one place to live in another
the birth rate of a country
items.markingKey: A. people moving from one place to live in another. Migration is a change of home

items.stem: Which of these is a pull factor for migrants?
items.markingKey: A. Better job opportunities. Pull factors attract people to a new place

items.stem: Explain one way migration can benefit the country that migrants leave.
items.answer: Migrants send money home (remittances) that supports families and the economy
options: Migrants send money home (remittances) that supports families and the economy
It always reduces skills at home
items.markingKey: B. Migrants send money home (remittances) that supports families and the economy. Remittances are a major income source for many countries

items.stem: The 'origin' of a source refers to
items.answer: who made it, when and where
items.subtopicHint: Evaluating sources: origin, purpose, value, limitation
options: who made it, when and where
items.markingKey: D. who made it, when and where. Origin helps judge reliability

items.stem: A government poster from 1940 asks citizens to save food for the war effort. What is one limitation of using it to find out how people actually felt?
items.answer: It shows what the government wanted people to think, not necessarily what they thought
items.subtopicHint: Evaluating sources: origin, purpose, value, limitation
options: It shows what the government wanted people to think, not necessarily what they thought
It is too old to be useful
items.markingKey: A. It shows what the government wanted people to think, not necessarily what they thought. Propaganda reveals intentions more than opinions

items.stem: Which set of sources gives the most balanced view of a protest?
items.answer: A police report, a protester's diary and a neutral newspaper
items.subtopicHint: Evaluating sources: origin, purpose, value, limitation
options: A police report, a protester's diary and a neutral newspaper
items.markingKey: C. A police report, a protester's diary and a neutral newspaper. Different perspectives can be cross-checked

items.stem: Sustainability means
items.answer: meeting present needs without harming future generations' ability to meet theirs
options: meeting present needs without harming future generations' ability to meet theirs
using resources as fast as possible
items.markingKey: C. meeting present needs without harming future generations' ability to meet theirs. This is the Brundtland definition

items.stem: Which is an example of a sustainable practice?
items.markingKey: C. Replanting trees after logging. Replanting replaces what was used

items.stem: A fishing community limits how many fish can be caught each year. Evaluate this policy.
items.answer: It protects fish stocks for the future, though it may lower income in the short term
options: It will make the fish extinct
It protects fish stocks for the future, though it may lower income in the short term
items.markingKey: C. It protects fish stocks for the future, though it may lower income in the short term. Evaluation weighs benefits against costs

items.stem: Urbanisation is
items.answer: the increasing share of people living in towns and cities
options: the increasing share of people living in towns and cities
items.markingKey: B. the increasing share of people living in towns and cities. Urban means towns and cities

items.stem: Which is a common problem in fast-growing cities?
items.markingKey: C. Traffic congestion and housing shortages. Infrastructure struggles to keep up

items.stem: Suggest the most effective long-term way for a city to reduce traffic congestion.
items.answer: Invest in reliable public transport and cycle lanes
options: Build more car parks in the centre
Invest in reliable public transport and cycle lanes
items.markingKey: C. Invest in reliable public transport and cycle lanes. Giving people alternatives reduces car trips

items.stem: What number comes next? 3, 7, 11, 15, ?
If 4 identical notebooks cost 96, what do 7 notebooks cost at the same rate?
25% of 80 is the same as 50% of which number?
What number comes next? 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
Book is to reading as fork is to ...
items.explanation: A book is used for reading; a fork is used for eating

items.stem: Which word does not belong with the others? apple, mango, carrot, banana
items.explanation: Carrot is a vegetable; the others are fruits

items.stem: All squares are rectangles. All rectangles have four sides. Which statement must be true?
options: Some rectangles do not have four sides
items.explanation: If every square is a rectangle and every rectangle has four sides, every square has four sides

items.stem: Asha is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Chitra. Dev is shorter than Chitra. Who is the shortest?
The shapes repeat in a pattern: circle, square, triangle, circle, square, ? Which shape comes next?
items.explanation: The three shapes repeat in the same order

items.stem: Figure 1 has 1 black dot, figure 2 has 2 white dots, figure 3 has 3 black dots, figure 4 has 4 white dots. What is figure 5?
items.explanation: One more dot each time; colours alternate

items.stem: Which letter comes next? A, C, F, J, O, ?
items.explanation: The gaps grow by one: +2, +3, +4, +5, then +6

items.stem: Rule: the third figure keeps the lines that appear in only one of the first two figures and drops lines they share. A vertical line '|' and a horizontal line '-' give a cross '+'. If figure 1 is a cross '+' and figure 2 is a vertical line '|', what is figure 3?
items.explanation: The vertical line is shared, so it is dropped; the horizontal line stays

items.stem: A square sheet of paper is folded in half once along a diagonal. What shape do you get?
items.explanation: The diagonal fold puts one corner on the opposite corner

items.stem: A mirror is held upright beside each capital letter. Which letter looks the same in the mirror?
items.explanation: A has a vertical line of symmetry

items.stem: A cube is painted on all faces and cut into 27 equal small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two painted faces?
items.explanation: Those are the middle cubes of the 12 edges

items.stem: You face north. You turn 90° clockwise, then 180°, then 90° anticlockwise. Which way do you face now?
